messages:
maya: quick heads-up — sunburst int8 bring-up looks off on the wiki_holdout. recall@10 down ~6pp vs fp16, clusters look squashed in UMAP :eyes:

sam: can you paste the eval numbers and the exact command you ran?

maya: sure — ran the usual eval harness: `eval_tool --model sunburst:int8:2026-03-18 --dataset wiki_holdout --metrics recall@1,5,10,mean_sim --batch 512`

maya: outputs: `recall@1: 0.42 (fp16 0.48), recall@5: 0.64 (fp16 0.70), recall@10: 0.72 (fp16 0.78), mean_cosine: 0.37 (fp16 0.44)`

liam: interesting — mean cosine drop suggests magnitude/norm change, not just local noise. did you normalize before indexing?

maya: yep, we L2-normalize after encoding for both variants. I checked a small sample: nearest neighbors for some queries flip types — semantically similar items pushed down.

anika: do we know quant params? per-tensor symmetric vs per-channel? int8 per-tensor often skews LayerNorm outputs.

maya: baseline int8 was per-tensor symmetric using the ONNX pipeline. trying per-channel now. also re-ran with euclidean and the drop is smaller but still present.

perf-bot: [regression-alert] model sunburst:int8:2026-03-18 triggered recall@10 drop of 6.1pp relative to production fp16 — alert created: #inc-5123

sam: possible fixes: 1) per-channel quantization on linear layers 2) add a tiny post-quant rescale learned on holdout (scalar) 3) increase embedding precision for final projection only (mixed-precision)

liam: also worth checking whitening/whiten-then-normalize pipeline — if quant introduces bias in certain dims, whitening might amplify it. run centroid shift and silhouette score comparisons: `centroid_shift.py --base fp16 --cand int8`

maya: running per-channel now. quick diagnostics: centroid L2 shift median = 0.12, mean sim shift per-cluster = -0.07. I'll attach UMAP screenshots when ready.

anika: if per-channel helps, try per-channel + clip range calibration with KL. sometimes calibration method matters more than symmetric range.

sam: also keep an eye on short queries (len<8) — we saw earlier short-query recall more sensitive. include stratified recall by qlen.

maya: good call — starting stratified run (short/med/long). will post numbers and diff table. planning: run pchannel+kl cal, pchannel+post-rescale, and mixed-precision final-proj. expect results by EOD. :thumbsup:

liam: thanks — if you want me to triage examples I can join after you post the NN diffs.

maya: will do. creating a ticket with steps and commands, linking to the perf-bot alert.
